title: Per‑tenant span aggregator using Cap'n Proto envelope and memory shedder
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Motivation:
High-throughput services (router, runtime pool) are generating millions of spans per minute. Current OTLP/JSON pipeline shows high CPU and network overhead and causes occasional head-of-line latency spikes during bursts. We need a lower-overhead, loss-tolerant aggregation layer that batches and encodes spans with a compact binary envelope to reduce per-span cost and smooth bursts per tenant.

Goal:
1) Implement an in-process per-tenant span aggregator that batches spans into a Cap'n Proto (capnp) envelope to minimize allocations and serialization overhead.
2) Add a memory shedder that drops low-priority spans when the aggregator memory exceeds configured cap, with configurable degradation strategy (drop-sampler, oldest-first, or priority-based).
3) Build a loss-tolerant forwarder that asynchronously writes batched envelopes to the collector, with optional on-disk spill-to-disk for short-term overloads and a converter service to translate capnp envelopes to OTLP/JSON for existing backends.
4) Make the feature behind a per-service feature flag and per-tenant opt-in so we can roll out gradually.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end throughput improvement: >=25% CPU reduction for the observability pipeline under a 10k req/s synthetic trace workload.
- Network bytes to collector reduced by >=35% for representative trace shapes.
- No increased p50/p95 latency for request path; p99 service tail should not regress more than 5%.
- Config knobs for memory cap, drop strategy, batch/window size, and disk spill path.
- Integration tests proving compatibility with existing Jaeger/OTLP collectors via the converter.

Design notes:
- Use a fixed-size ring buffer per-tenant for incoming span references, with a background serializer that encodes capnp envelopes directly into preallocated byte slices. Avoid per-span heap allocations where possible.
- Memory shedder runs when aggregate buffered bytes exceed tenant_memory_cap; shedder selects spans to drop based on priority tag (if present), otherwise oldest-first. Shedder should emit a metric counter with shed reasons.
- Forwarder will group multiple tenant envelopes into a single outbound request when routing to the same collector to reduce connection churn.
- For compatibility, implement a small converter microservice that accepts capnp envelopes and emits OTLP/HTTP to our existing collectors during rollout. Converter lives in runtime-tools/trace-converter.
- Rollout via feature flag CF=env.FRONTEND_SPAN_AGGREGATOR with per-service override and a gating comparative metric in grafana dashboard.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Collector incompatibility — mitigation: converter service + canary with test tenants and dedicated collector instance.
- Risk: Memory leaks / unbounded buffers — mitigation: hard memory cap, eviction + disk spill, e2e chaos tests.
- Risk: Observability signal loss during sheds — mitigation: expose shed metrics, wire into incident->alerting, and implement conservative default drop rates.
comments: 2026-03-06 - Spike complete: prototype in runtime/collector-poc showed ~32% CPU reduction in serialization stage and ~38% network bytes reduction on our synthetic span generator. Test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2987 (POC branch, do not merge).

2026-03-07 - Design review with Observability: agreed on capnp as intermediate envelope and converter service approach. Confluence notes: https://confluence.redwood.com/pages/spans-aggregator. Rajat volunteered to own the eviction strategy implementation.
2026-03-08 - Implementation started: added per-tenant ring buffer skeleton and initial capnp schemas under runtime/trace/format. Running unit tests locally for zero-copy serializer.

2026-03-09 - Code review feedback (PR #3002): reviewers asked for metrics shapes, clear shed reason labels, and backpressure test coverage. Left TODOs to add metric names per instrumentation guidelines. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3002

2026-03-10 - Load test with 50% sampling shape: aggregator + converter combo reduced average egress sockets by ~22% and reduced collector QPS variability. Observability dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.com/grafana/d/obs/collector-throughput (private).

2026-03-11 - Perf tuning: adjusted default batch window to 50ms for a better latency/efficiency tradeoff after spike; dropped from 100ms to 50ms to reduce buffer-local latency under low-throughput tenants. Noted increase in CPU for tiny tenants — added per-tenant batching config so low-volume tenants bypass aggregator to avoid overhead.

2026-03-12 - Next steps: add disk spill implementation with max_spill_mb per tenant, e2e tests that simulate collector downtime, and prepare canary rollout plan (start with internal infra tenants then opt-in external customers). Planned follow-ups: create ENG-150101 (disk-spill e2e), ENG-150202 (canary rollout runbook).
